articles.title: Helping robots fit into the human workplace
articles.summary: Founded by Anthony Jules ’92, SM ’92 and Professor Emeritus Rodney Brooks, Robust AI’s robots are designed to collaborate with humans in factories and warehouses.

Despite fears about robots replacing humans at work, there are still plenty of things humans can do far better than machines. That’s fine with Robust AI, a startup building robots designed to complement what humans do best.

The company’s mobile robot, named Carter, resembles a utility cart on wheels and is designed to fit seamlessly alongside humans in fast-changing warehouse and factory environments. Carter features a force-sensitive handlebar for easy guidance, an AI-powered vision system, and holonomic wheels for instant movement in any direction.
As a result, humans can cut Carter off, push and pull it in any direction with one hand, and direct it with gestures or the onboard touch screen.

articles.title: New AI “copilot” helps engineers design better structures
articles.summary: The system asks humans for feedback to increase trust in machine-generated designs for buildings and bridges.

The use of algorithms to design structures has led to new parts optimized for ultralight aircraft, high-bandwidth antennas, and F1 racing cars.

But the best algorithmic design techniques still require lots of computation and time: Users only see the final design after it’s complete, after which they often must start the design process all over again to make changes. That process also makes it harder to trust that the final designs are structurally sound.

MIT researchers are making algorithmic designs more collaborative with a system that acts like an AI copilot. As the algorithm is generating the structure, it presents regions to the human designer for feedback.

articles.title: No, AI agents did not discover a previously unknown Maya site
articles.summary: Armed with a team of AI agents, Google researcher Pietro Miotti claimed earlier this week to have discovered a potentially unmapped Maya site in Mexico. There was just one problem: The site had already been discovered and was published in an academic journal last year.
body: Scientists are getting tired of amateurs parachuting into their fields and making ‘discoveries’ with AI.
Local communities are often already well aware of sites in their area.

Miotti said the idea to use AI to search for archeological sites came to him while traveling in Peru, when he began wondering what historic explorers might do with access to modern technology. He settled on lidar, a laser-based mapping technology that can produce detailed three-dimensional images of the environment, and set a team of 48 AI agents to comb through NASA lidar data for signs of undocumented sites. As “Peru isn’t well covered” by public lidar data, Miotti wrote, he shifted his focus to the Maya region.
points: Armed with a team of AI agents, Google researcher Pietro Miotti claimed earlier this week to have discovered a potentially unmapped Maya site in Mexico.

articles.title: Three Lincoln Laboratory technologies receive 2026 R&D 100 Awards
articles.summary: A secure operating system, a quantum microsystem platform, and a 5G interference-canceling algorithm are named among the year's most significant innovations.
body: Three technologies developed by MIT Lincoln Laboratory are among recipients of 2026 R&D 100 Awards. The awards recognize the 100 most significant innovations that have transitioned to use or been made available for license in the past year.

R&D World, an online publication, manages the awards program, which has run annually since 1963. The worldwide competition is judged by an independent panel of science and technology experts and industry professionals.

The laboratory's winners overcome obstacles to improving the security and capability of systems. One technology is an operating system designed to protect embedded computers from cyberattacks. Another technology is a platform for integrating superconductor and semiconductor chips in a wafer-scale system for quantum or high-performance computing. The final winner is an algorithm that removes interference 5G base stations incur on co-channel radio frequency (RF) devices.
points: A secure operating system, a quantum microsystem platform, and a 5G interference-canceling algorithm are named among the year's most significant innovations.

articles.title: The Jensen Huang scandal is hardly over
articles.summary: I was certain, until the story of Jensen Huang's second affair hit, that Huang was bulletproof. After all, why wouldn't he be? He's placed himself indispensably at the center of the AI industry and famously had no succession plan at Nvidia. In fact, he's the only CEO Nvidia has ever had.
body: A second affair has hit the news cycle, but that’s not what matters here.

Then two stories were published nearly back to back on Wednesday: one alleging Huang had an affair with his subordinate Kimberly Powell, another that the board was meeting to consider his ouster. First thing Thursday morning, Nvidia announced Huang had resigned. One of the most powerful men in Silicon Valley was out.
Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46.

Even months before the report that Alice “No Relation” Huang, an exec at Megaspeed, was having an affair with Huang, there were questions about Nvidia’s business in China. The US government has placed strict export controls on Nvidia’s high-end chips. Huang claimed in May that as a result, Nvidia has zero percent market share in China. But also in May, short sellers Culper Research published a report in which they wrote, “We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia’s FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China – supported both by illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries.”

articles.title: Silicon Valley Is Still Defending Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia employees and tech insiders never thought the chip king would lose his job. Despite his sudden resignation, many of them are still in denial.
body: News of Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security was first met with a muted response in Silicon Valley —including inside Nvidia itself. Huang’s resignation, after news of two other alleged romantic relationships with Nvidia staffers, has left both the company and the broader AI industry stunned.

As revelations about Huang’s initial affair came out earlier this week, rank-and-file Nvidia employees at first pursued business as usual, according to two current and three former employees at the chipmaker, speaking anonymously to protect relationships at the company. They trusted the board to investigate and act accordingly, but few workers thought Huang would actually leave.

Nvidia’s roughly 60,000 employees are loyal to the point that its global turnover rate is reportedly among the lowest in tech. Workers say they have heard it called having “green in your blood” or being “green-pilled” or on “team green,” referring to the company’s signature color. Huang was the company’s soul and the founder who stuck with it through challenges for 33 years. Employees appreciated that he kept layoffs rare and red tape sparing.
points: Nvidia employees and tech insiders never thought the chip king would lose his job.
Despite his sudden resignation, many of them are still in denial.

articles.title: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
articles.summary: Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including "questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests." The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses.
body: Google’s Robby Stein says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is ‘the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.’

Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen also gives users a wider range of links in its responses by “conducting simultaneous queries across all the relevant subtopics.” Its responses have more visuals, too, like images, comparison tables, graphs, and maps. One of Stein’s examples shows the AI generating an interactive animated driving simulation in response to a user’s question about how phones locate which lane of a highway a car is on in areas without cell service. Google says the new model also has improved language understanding “across all supported AI Mode languages.”

Users have more thinking level options with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, as well, including low, medium, high, and a new “xhigh” mode. According to Google, the new model “delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence” compared to Gemini Flash 3.8, and it “matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class,” like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.

articles.title: Jensen Huang Didn’t Name His Own Replacement as One of Tech’s Most Powerful Women
articles.summary: A recent WIRED investigation explored the complicated definition of “power” for women in the industry. Jensen Huang’s answers now appear to show his blind spots.
body: The most powerful woman in tech at this very moment is Colette Kress, the new interim CEO of Nvidia —but her predecessor, Jensen Huang, failed to mention her in a recent back-and-forth about the topic.

Earlier this fall, WIRED published a feature story exploring the complex topic of power for women working in an industry traditionally dominated by men. We questioned why Silicon Valley doesn't have an Elon-esque or Jensen-like female hero (or villain) and determined that the rubric of power still looks different for women, whether they manage to hold significant financial capital, flex their political prowess, dictate cultural norms, or run intellectual circles around the industry.

We also determined there wasn’t just one singular impressive woman in tech, but a whole lot of them: Lisa Su, Gwynne Shotwell, Laurene Powell Jobs, and dozens more. Kress, then-CFO of Nvidia, was also given a nod.
As part of the reporting process, WIRED wanted to include the insights of a few established men in Silicon Valley. So we emailed Huang directly to ask for his thoughts.

articles.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
articles.summary: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were…
body: Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”
But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them.

articles.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
articles.summary: MIT scientists developed a training method to generate models that simulate the effects of human activities on climate much more quickly than other approaches.
body: Accurate, up-to-date climate projections are essential for planning decisions that enhance the resilience of power grids, protect public health, maximize agricultural yields, and more.
Now, MIT researchers have developed a technique that streamlines the production of fast, trustworthy, and adaptable artificial intelligence models for climate prediction.
These specialized AI models, known as climate emulators, can rapidly simulate the effects of human activities onto a future climate, predicting impacts on temperatures or sea level, for example.

Because emulators run in a matter of seconds, scientists use them to efficiently test thousands of varied climate scenarios. This provides more reliable estimates and can identify unexpected outcomes of regional interventions.

articles.title: How Amplitude ships product improvements in 1–2 days with OpenAI
articles.summary: Built primarily on OpenAI models, Amplitude’s proactive product agent, Wave, identifies what to build, helps teams ship changes with coding agents, and measures the impact.
body: Lower mean model cost per dispatch for GPT‑6.1 Sol in Amplitude’s Data Science Agent evaluation.

Amplitude has always helped teams see how people actually use their products. Its proactive product agent Wave helps teams turn those insights into shipped improvements. Amplitude describes Wave as roughly 80% powered by OpenAI models, including GPT‑6.1 Sol, GPT‑6 Luna, and GPT‑Image‑2.5 Flare. Wave turns product insights into implementation plans teams can ship to coding agents, including Codex, then measures the impact.

Amplitude estimates that Wave can help teams ship product improvements in 1–2 days, down from roughly a month. On Amplitude’s own homepage, Wave helped personalize suggestion cards, driving a 160% lift in card-driven sends.

Wave is Amplitude’s proactive product agent. Teams give it a product area and the goals and metrics they want to improve. Wave brings together Amplitude data, session replays, customer feedback, and code to identify and prioritize opportunities, develop solutions, and coordinate implementation with people and coding agents. It then tracks outcomes and uses those learnings to inform the next round of improvements.
